title: Final-Theory Bench v0.3.9: clone-reproducible exact d=2 certificate bundle
description: A reproducible exact-symbolic certificate bundle for the repository's frozen n<=4 strong-operator CPOBC compiler. Version 0.3.8 carries forward the v0.3.7 theorem that nonsingular d=2 literal-branch solutions have commuting Q1 through Q4 on the recorded denominator-open locus. The proof remains the Q5-free 21-chart QQ saturation campaign, with two finite-field campaigns retained only as scouts, plus the separate exact scalar-chain identity certificate. Version 0.3.8 changed no scientific verdict: it canonicalised tracked text to LF and supplied a field-aware bridge for 1,007 historical raw-byte bindings to 207 CRLF-era artifacts. Version 0.3.9 likewise changes no scientific verdict: the v0.3 baseline audit resolves the frozen branch through the remote-tracking ref that a full clone with an 'origin' remote provides, so verification no longer depends on a local branch created by hand on the authoring machine. The unrestricted theory remains open. OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, test scaffolding, artifact checks, and prose; Anthropic Claude assisted with research design, the Q5-free proof strategy, symbolic cross-checks, and prior-art review. The human author selected the scope and resource budgets, reviewed the work, and remains responsible for every claim; AI systems are not authors. This deposit is a curated bundle of the 203 files named by results/v0.3.9_release_manifest.json, not a repository snapshot. Third-party material is deliberately excluded and is not covered by the MIT licence: the 52 PDFs under references/papers/, the 52 extracted texts under references/text/, and the vendored archives under oracle/sage_periods/vendor/. Those sources are identified in references/sources.json by DOI, URL, retrieval date and SHA-256, so they can be obtained from their publishers and checked against the recorded digests. Full verification additionally requires the git repository, because the baseline audits resolve commits, tags and a branch; see REPRODUCING_v0.3.9.md.
